items.description: Condition contains details for one aspect of the current state of this API Resource

lastTransitionTime.description: lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description: message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description: observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description: reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. --- Many .condition.type values are consistent across resources like Available, but because arbitrary conditions can be useful (see .node.status.conditions), the ability to deconflict is important. The regex it matches is (dns1123SubdomainFmt/)?(qualifiedNameFmt)

additionalProperties.description: Status specifies the status of an operand. And operand manages resources, some of which are not immediately available and need their status monitored, such as Deployments, Daemonsets, Ingressess etc. Some resources are immediately available and should not be monitored once accepted by the cluster, such as Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets etc. If all resources of an operand are ready, a Status with Ready set to 'true' and a nil 'Reasons' slice should be returned, otherwise, a Status with 'Reasons' slice containig the reason why the Operand is not ready (Deployment pods are not ready for example.)

lastTransitionTime.description: LastTransitionTime specifies the last time the operand readiness changed

NetworkTopologyLabelsOptional.description: A list of Kubernetes node label key/value pairs that represent the node’s position in the cluster’s network topology (for example, region, zone, block, rack, or hostname). The topology is attached to the node pool on which the workload runs. The label order represents the hierarchy, from farthest (first) to closest (last). These labels are used by the NVIDIA Run:ai Scheduler when making placement decisions.

GpuPodsPlacementStrategy.description: Defines the placement strategy for GPU pods within the node pool.

node.description:
Specifies how GPU pods are placed across nodes.
 - binpack - Place as many GPU pods as possible on each node to use fewer nodes and maximize available capacity.
 - spread - Distribute GPU pods across as many nodes as possible to balance load across nodes.

device.description:
Specifies how GPU pods are placed across GPU devices within a node when using GPU fractions.
 - binpack - Place as many GPU pods as possible on each GPU device to use fewer devices and maximize available capacity, minimizing GPU fraction fragmentation.
 - spread - Distribute GPU pods across as many GPU devices as possible to balance load across devices.

CpuPodsPlacementStrategy.description: Defines the placement strategy for CPU pods within the node pool.

node.description:
Specifies how CPU pods are placed across nodes.
 - binpack - Place as many CPU pods as possible on each node to use fewer nodes and maximize available capacity.
 - spread - Distribute CPU pods across as many nodes as possible to balance load across nodes.

TimeBasedFairShareWindowType.description:
The method for evaluating the usage window.
 - sliding: A moving window that always evaluates the most recent time period. For example, a 7-day sliding window always considers the last 7 days.
 - tumbling: Fixed, non-overlapping intervals that reset at the end of each cycle. Requires tumblingWindowStartTime to define the cycle anchor.

TimeBasedFairShare.description: Time-based fairshare configuration for the node pool. [Experimental].

enabled.description: Enables time-based fairshare for the node pool. When true, the Scheduler adjusts fairshare based on historical resource usage over a defined time window, allowing past consumption to influence scheduling order. When false, scheduling is based only on the current queue state. [Experimental]

historicalUsageWeight.description:
Set the weight value that determines how a project’s historical resource usage affects its fairshare.
 - 0.0: Ignore historical usage data (100% current usage).
 - 1.0: Historical usage data has higher impact, it may cause fairshare to be 0.
 - Values between 0.0 and 1.0 combine historical and current usage to maintain a balanced fairshare
 - Values above 1 will cause historical usage to have an even higher impact on fairshare.

decayHalfLife.description:
Set the half-life time to define the decay rate of a project’s historical resource usage. The half-life defines how long it takes for past usage to diminish to half of its original influence on a project's fairshare.
 - 0: disables decay; all historical usage is weighted equally.
 - > 0: older usage gradually contributes less over time (e.g., with a 24-hour half-life, usage from 24 hours ago contributes 50%, from 48 hours ago 25%, and so on).

windowDuration.description: The time period over which historical usage is evaluated. Only usage within this window contributes to fairshare. For sliding windows, this is a moving period (e.g., 7d = always the last 7 days). For tumbling windows, this is the fixed cycle duration after which the window resets.

tumblingWindowStartTime.description:
An RFC-3339 timestamp that defines the start time for all tumbling windows. Used only when windowType = Tumbling. This timestamp marks the beginning of the first fixed window, and subsequent windows repeat at intervals equal to the configured WindowDuration.
For example, with a 7-day window, an anchor of 2025-01-06T08:00:00Z produces weekly windows starting every Monday at 08:00 UTC.

placementStrategy.description:
Deprecated. Use gpuPodsPlacementStrategy and cpuPodsPlacementStrategy instead.
On write, when a new field is provided it takes precedence over the equivalent field here.
On read, both this field and the new fields are returned; this field reflects the node-level strategies.

minGuaranteedRuntime.description: Minimum duration (e.g., 5d8h40m) that a preemptible workload is guaranteed to run once scheduled and bound to a node. During this period, it is considered non-preemptible even if a higher-priority workload becomes eligible. Defaults to 0 (immediate preemption allowed).

numaAwareScheduling.description: When enabled, the Scheduler places workloads so that GPU, CPU, and CPU memory are allocated within the same NUMA node where possible, minimizing cross-NUMA fragmentation and improving performance. Requires the NodeResourceTopology (NRT) component and a Topology Manager policy other than 'none' on the pool's nodes. When disabled, the Scheduler places workloads using aggregate node capacity only, without considering NUMA topology.

The state of the configuration. The possible values are:
Updating - The control plane got a request to update the cluster configuration and did not receive a status update yet from the cluster.
Applying - The configuration has been stored on the cluster, but is not yet applied.
Applied - The configuration has been successfully applied in the cluster.
Failed - The cluster has failed to apply the configuration.

lastTransitionTime.description: lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description: message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.

reason.description: reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. --- Many .condition.type values are consistent across resources like Available, but because arbitrary conditions can be useful (see .node.status.conditions), the ability to deconflict is important.
